nodes.summary: The extinction probability is the only `[0, 1]`-valued solution `q` on `[0, ∞)` of the backward equation `q' = d - (b + d) q + b q²` with `q 0 = 0`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the extinction probability solving the backward equation

nodes.summary: Kendall's extinction probability `α t = P(X t = 0 | X 0 = 1)` of the linear birth–death process with per-capita birth rate `b` and death rate `d`: `d (E - 1) / (b E - d)` with `E = exp ((b - d) t)` if `b ≠ d`, and `b t / (1 + b t)` if `b = d`. Meaningful for `0 ≤ b`, `0 ≤ d`, `0 ≤ t`.
nodes.title: Kendall's extinction probability for the birth–death process

nodes.summary: Kendall's ratio `β t` of the geometric tail of the law of `X t`: `b (E - 1) / (b E - d)` with `E = exp ((b - d) t)` if `b ≠ d`, and `b t / (1 + b t)` if `b = d`.
nodes.title: Kendall's geometric tail ratio

nodes.summary: Backward Kolmogorov equation for the extinction probability: `α' = d - (b + d) α + b α²` (Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4).
nodes.title: Backward Kolmogorov equation for the extinction probability

nodes.summary: Forward Kolmogorov equation for state `n + 1`: `p_(n+1)' = b n p_n - (b + d) (n + 1) p_(n+1) + d (n + 2) p_(n+2)`.
nodes.title: Forward Kolmogorov equation for positive states

nodes.summary: Forward Kolmogorov equation for state `0`: `p_0' = d p_1`.
nodes.title: Forward Kolmogorov equation for the empty state

nodes.summary: The mean population size at time `t` started from one individual is `E[X t] = exp ((b - d) t)` (Kendall 1948; Bailey 1964, ch. 8).
nodes.title: Mean population size of the linear birth–death process

nodes.summary: Kendall's probabilities sum to `1`: no mass escapes to infinity.
nodes.title: Kendall's probabilities sum to one

nodes.summary: At time `0` the population is one individual: `prob b d 0 = δ₁`.
nodes.title: Linear birth–death law at time zero

nodes.summary: Kendall's law of the linear birth–death process at time `t` started from one individual: `prob b d t 0 = α t` and `prob b d t (n + 1) = (1 - α t) (1 - β t) (β t) ^ n`.
nodes.title: Kendall's law of the linear birth–death process

nodes.summary: Critical and subcritical cases: if `b ≤ d` and `0 < d`, extinction is certain in the limit.
nodes.title: Certain extinction in the critical and subcritical cases

nodes.summary: Supercritical case: if `d < b`, the extinction probability tends to `d / b`.
nodes.title: Limiting extinction probability in the supercritical case

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
